subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should it be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or kept behind a narrower policy surface?
rationale: This changes an SSRF boundary and public config contract; source code shows the primitive exists, but policy shape, authorization, and hard-deny behavior require maintainer/security intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve scoped nested SSRF policy
options.body: Add a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` capability with dangerous naming, metadata/link-local rules, cache isolation, redirect checks, audit output, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Fold into broader egress design
options.body: Pause this specific flag and resolve it through the broader web-tool allow/deny egress policy at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685.

options.title: Route through broader egress policy
options.body: Fold this into the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, domain allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped nested SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Add a default-off `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` capability with dangerous naming, metadata/link-local rules, cache isolation, redirect checks, audit output, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the clearest maintainer-visible security-policy signal on this exact issue and have the strongest sampled adjacent SSRF history.
